title: Frequency-addressed modal cell: the field as compressed computational matter
summary: This pass records a cross-family synthesis that only became explicit after the resonance, field-computing, computational-matter, NSSN and structural-compiler lines were viewed together. Earlier projects mostly chose a wave/field substrate and asked what it could compute. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell reverses that direction: start from an already-interesting resonant, state-dependent receiver and ask what smaller operator description survives compression. v0 shows that state compression is not mechanism compression: rank-8 POD captures 99.86% of a 36-state teacher while naive nonlinear closure fails autonomous rollout. v1 extends the object through branching axonal matter with deliberately weak local ephaptic timing. v2 shows frozen branching collapses exactly to a sparse fixed-delay graph; only runtime-dependent timing survives that attacker. v3 then imports one useful abstraction from wetware computing without importing organoid biology: hide the substrate internals and learn a stimulation language through sparse external ports. FANMC learns a robust four-symbol persistent code, but a linear state-space reservoir nearly matches it; space alone is perfect, frequency alone still carries a weaker one-port code, and phase alone falls near chance. The resulting wall lesson is narrower and stronger: computational matter should be judged by what externally controllable operator survives ordinary reduced, graph, reservoir and address-ablation attackers. v4 then asks whether the stimulation language can be discovered cheaply: with only 12 of 96 candidate interventions, active, fixed-cover, random and exhaustive selection all reach perfect six-symbol accuracy, so response-adaptive probe efficiency is not established. The only surviving adaptive residue is geometric margin: the active codebook's median minimum response separation is about 2.15x random. That margin is now a hypothesis to spend under drift, not a win by itself. v5 spends that margin under frozen substrate drift and kills the hypothesis that the wider active code is more robust: active and random codebooks fail and recover together. A geometry/interface shift sends both from perfect decoding to six-class chance, but one measurement of the new unwritten baseline restores both to perfect median decoding. The stronger surviving lesson is coordinate-relative reuse: the external language is much more stable as a displacement from the current baseline than as an absolute response vector.

nodes.claim: Tests whether rich receiving/transmitting matter can be compressed and externally programmed through sparse stimulation ports, while preserving only the runtime-dependent computation that survives reduced-state, graph, reservoir and address-ablation attackers.
nodes.survived: v0 establishes strong state compressibility (rank-8 POD energy 0.998602). v1 adds grown branching axonal routes and weak local coactivity-dependent timing. v2 isolates the static-graph boundary. v3 hides the population internals behind eight stimulation/recording ports and learns a four-symbol external write/read code: full FANMC reaches 1.000 held-out accuracy after a 96-step wait, while removing the slow material write falls to 0.1875. With one electrode fixed, frequency-only writes retain 0.8125 accuracy; frequency+phase reaches 0.9167. v4 shows that a six-symbol language can be discovered with only 12/96 purchased probes in all tested selectors, and the response-adaptive selector produces a larger median minimum code separation (0.001040 versus 0.000483 random and 0.000387 fixed cover). v5 shows that the six-symbol language can survive synthetic geometry and combined geometry+dynamics drift in baseline-relative coordinates: although absolute decoding collapses to 0.1667 under geometry shift, one measurement of the new unwritten baseline restores both active and random codebooks to 1.000 median accuracy without replaying any symbol. Recurrent-gain drift remains 1.000 zero-shot.
nodes.killed: v0's naive nonlinear modal closure fails autonomous held-out rollout. v2 kills any claim that branching geometry alone is a new primitive because the frozen arbor is exactly reducible to a sparse fixed-delay graph. v3 kills a first architecture-advantage claim: a 48-state linear state-space reservoir reaches 0.9792 through the identical black-box interface, and spatial-only FANMC reaches 1.000, so frequency is not necessary for the easiest four-symbol task. Phase-only addressing is 0.2708, near four-class chance. The result is a programming/interface mechanism, not superiority to conventional recurrent state. v4 kills the first active-probe-efficiency claim: active, fixed-cover, random and exhaustive search all reach 1.000 median six-symbol accuracy, with zero active world wins by accuracy. The larger active response margin is not promoted to utility until it survives drift or harsher noise. v5 kills the proposed utility of v4's wider active code under the tested drifts: active and random codebooks have the same median zero-shot and recalibrated accuracy, so the ~2.15x larger minimum pair separation did not buy measurable robustness. Two-code-anchor recalibration also proves unnecessary for these drift worlds because a one-baseline recenter attacker repairs the code just as well.

edges.why: The new repository explicitly builds its teacher from the NotSoSimpleNeuron quasi-active frequency gate plus the later synthetic local voltage-dependent interaction, then asks whether those resident state-conditioned dynamics admit a much smaller autonomous modal surrogate.

Entrain already made frequency an executable routing coordinate and measured its Arnold-tongue resolution limit. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell keeps frequency/phase as the probe address but changes the scientific direction from constructing oscillator matter to reducing an existing richer receiver.

InformationFlow demonstrated WHERE/WHICH/SIGN selection through spatial overlap, frequency and phase but supplied its useful nonlinear coupling explicitly. The new reduction experiment asks whether useful state-dependent coupling can instead be extracted from richer computational matter rather than written into the field law by hand.

Operaattori shows the forward reduction idea on real morphology: complicated physical structure can compile to compact transport and nonlinear operator objects. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell applies the analogous compression question to a resonant state-dependent synthetic receiver, without claiming direct ancestry or that the v0 teacher is Operaattori's biological model.

v3 turns the substrate into a hidden machine that can only be programmed by choosing interventions and reading consequences. That is the same active-identification grammar AnotherOddThing isolates, now applied to discovering a reusable stimulation code rather than selecting among explicit hypotheses.

ReadWrite studies what a bounded observer can reveal by applying known writes. v3 makes that constraint the programming interface itself: internal FANMC state is hidden, and only sparse port-level stimulation plus later readout is legal. v5 sharpens the observer lesson: an apparent catastrophic code failure can come from a shifted measurement origin rather than changed symbol-relative computation; measuring the new unwritten baseline can restore the old language without re-identifying its writes.

motifs.title: The field is no longer the hypothesis; it is a reduced representation of computational matter
motifs.description: Earlier field and oscillator projects usually started by choosing a field law and exploring the computation it could support. Operaattori, NotSoSimpleNeuron and FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell point in the reverse direction: begin with a richer physical or synthetic receiver, identify what operator family it actually implements, and try to compress that family into a smaller executable object. The v0 failure sharpens the rule: a compact state manifold is not enough; the reduced law must remain causal and stable when run autonomously on interventions it did not fit.

motifs.title: Frequency can address a resident operator, but filtering alone is not enough
motifs.description: SpectralNeuron establishes the boring floor: resonance supplies finite FDM-style addressing. Entrain adds measured entrainment routing and phase relations. InformationFlow uses frequency/phase/spatial overlap to select a nonlinear write. NotSoSimpleNeuron then shows the stronger receiver-side object: active resident state changes cross-mode coupling and the operator encountered by the next event. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell asks whether that stronger object can be compressed while keeping frequency/phase as the external address rather than confusing a band-pass filter with the computation itself.

motifs.title: A compressed representation earns mechanism status only when it survives new interventions
motifs.description: MatrixInMatrix already separates a compact harmonic reconstruction from the source dynamics that heal and evolve. NeuralAlgorithmDecoding requires an executable causal surrogate rather than a pretty hidden geometry. FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell makes the same boundary dynamical: rank-8 coordinates explain almost all sampled state variance, yet a locally better nonlinear transition fit fails when autonomously rolled through unseen frequencies, tone pairs and histories. Representation compression and mechanism compression are different gates. v5 adds a related identification boundary: a changed absolute observation is not evidence that the hidden computation changed. After geometry drift, the apparent language failure is repaired by updating only the response origin, so intervention-stable relative geometry is more diagnostic than raw coordinates.

motifs.title: Frozen structure can collapse to a graph; runtime-dependent matter is the surviving residue
motifs.description: The axonal extension creates a useful correction to the structure-as-computation story. Development can manufacture a branching route, but once that geometry is frozen and conduction is context-free, a sparse graph with fixed delays reproduces terminal arrival timing exactly. What survives the attacker is not branching itself but the weak dependence of propagation timing on nearby co-active axonal matter. This keeps the claim narrow: physical structure may determine the operator, while runtime material state determines whether the operator is richer than a static graph representation.

motifs.title: Do not program hidden matter by writing its internals; learn an external intervention language
motifs.description: The FinalSpark wetware-computing interface motivates a useful abstraction even after the biology is removed: internal parameters may be inaccessible while the substrate remains controllable through a small set of stimulation/recording ports. FANMC v3 implements that constraint synthetically. A controller learns a write/read code only from externally observed consequences. The slow-state ablation establishes that persistent FANMC writes need resident hidden state, but the linear-reservoir attacker shows the interface itself is not uniquely biological. Address ablations further separate coordinates: space is strongest here; frequency alone remains a usable one-port address; phase alone does not. v4 adds the cost boundary: at a 12/96 probe budget the task saturates for active, fixed-cover and random selection alike, so adaptive experiment choice has not yet earned a sample-efficiency claim. Active selection does yield roughly twice the minimum response-space separation of random; the next discriminating experiment is whether that unused margin becomes useful when the hidden substrate drifts. v5 then kills the tempting interpretation that v4's wider active code must be more robust. Under a synthetic geometry/interface shift, both active and random absolute codebooks collapse from 1.000 to 0.1667, and both recover to 1.000 after recentering on a single measurement of the new unwritten baseline. The reusable object is therefore relational: store each symbol as a displacement from the current baseline, not as an absolute response vector. In this family, tracking the observer frame is cheaper than relearning the hidden matter.
